level_1_deduction.introText: These two rocks look like identical pieces of gold. Let's find out if Chang sent us real Gold, or if it's a trick!

questions.text: 1. Why shouldn't we identify a mineral just by looking at its outside color?

options.label: Because gold is invisible in the dark.
Because impurities or weather can change the surface color.
Because minerals change color every day.

questions.text: 2. When I rubbed the mineral on the unglazed porcelain tile, the 'streak' it left behind was actually...
3. What happens if a mineral is harder than the ceramic streak plate?

options.label: It leaves a very dark streak.
It scratches the plate and leaves no streak.

questions.text: 4. Real gold is 'malleable'. When I hit it with the hammer, what did it do?

items.desc: The Zlatanium. Small but incredibly dense.

items.desc_shake:
JINGLE! JANGLE!
Haddock: 'Blistering Barnacles! I left a bag of gold coins in the pocket!'
(You remove the coins. Now the coat is High Volume, but Low Mass!)
items.descAlt:
Haddock's wool coat.
Now lighter after you shook off the coins

items.desc: A golden bust of the Captain. Looks expensive.
items.desc_inspect:
It looks like solid gold... but wait! You peel a corner. It's actually hollow chocolate wrapped in foil!
It takes up a lot of Space (Volume), but has very little Weight (Mass).

items.desc: Dry sea sponges. Soft and light.

questions.text: Physics? Is he a suspect? We’d better update our notes, Thompson. Tintin, why did the rock fall through instead of just being heavy?

options.label: Because the rock is actually a termite in disguise.
Because its heavy mass was concentrated into a tiny, sharp area, creating massive Pressure.
Because the canvas bag was allergic to the rock.

questions.text: Tintin's Correction: The sugar was carried away and mixed. The Zlatanium just melted; its 'people' are still all there, just sliding around. This is a...
The Diva asks: 'If the Capitaine cools the water, will my soup turn back into a hard stone?'
Captain, why can we easily pull the iron out of the mud, but the tweezers failed on the heated crystal?

options.label: Because Iron atoms are naturally heavier than Sulfur atoms.
In the mud, their outer shells just bumped together. In the heated crystal, their shells merged to form a completely new, rigid structure!
Because the mud is wet, making the atoms slippery.

questions.text: Captain Haddock thinks the blue crystals magically teleported into the pan. Professor Calculus says they reappeared because:

options.label: They were hiding inside the wire mesh of the sieve.
They were dissolved. Boiling the water forced them to turn back into solids.
The heat lamp melted them and they froze again.

questions.text: In the centrifuge, why did the muddy gold sink all the way to the very bottom of the test tube, while the sand stayed in the middle?

options.label: Gold has a much higher density than sand.
Gold is heavier because it is magnetic.
The sand was pushed up by the blue crystals.

questions.text: Why did we need to dissolve the mixture in water before putting it in the Centrifuge?

options.label: Because the centrifuge needs water to cool down its engine.
Because water makes the gold heavier.
Because atoms in a dry solid are stuck together. The liquid gave them freedom to slide past each other and sort by weight!

questions.text: What chemical property allowed us to separate the blue crystals from the sand just by adding water?

options.label: Evaporation: The water made the crystals evaporate into the air.
Solubility: The crystals dissolve in water, but the sand is insoluble.
Density: The water made the sand heavier so it fell out.

questions.text: After all the magnets, water, spinning, and heating... the Gold Plate stayed exactly the same. What does that tell us?

options.label: It is a mixture of water and sand.
It is a pure Element. It doesn't break down or react easily!

quizPool.prompt: What does a mineral's 'Luster' describe?
quizPool.explanation: Luster is simply the way a mineral reflects light from its surface, making it look shiny, dull, or metallic.

quizPool.prompt: Why is Luster a bad way to identify real gold?
quizPool.explanation: Many minerals, like Pyrite (Fool's Gold), have the exact same shiny, metallic surface as real gold, fooling the eyes.

options.label: Other minerals can look exactly like it

quizPool.prompt: When Tintin rubs the mineral on a ceramic tile, what is he testing?
quizPool.explanation: He is performing a Streak Test, which reveals the true color of the mineral in its powdered form.
quizPool.learnMoreText: 🎥 Watch: The Streak Test in Geology

quizPool.prompt: What happens if you hit a real gold nugget with a hammer?
quizPool.explanation: Real gold is highly malleable, meaning it will flatten or change shape instead of shattering.

quizPool.prompt: Why did the 'gold' nugget shatter when Tintin tapped it?
quizPool.explanation: The nugget was Pyrite, which is brittle. Unlike malleable gold, brittle minerals break or shatter under pressure.

quizPool.prompt: Which tool can easily separate iron nails from a pile of non-magnetic junk?
quizPool.explanation: A magnet uses a magnetic field to attract ferromagnetic materials like iron and steel.

quizPool.prompt: Why did the dull grey Zlatanium rock crack the mahogany pedestal?
quizPool.explanation: The rock has extremely high density, meaning it has a massive amount of mass packed into a very small volume.

quizPool.prompt: How did Professor Calculus explain density using suitcases?
quizPool.explanation: Density is mass per unit volume. A suitcase full of lead has more mass in the same space (volume) than a suitcase of feathers.

options.label: Lead atoms are bigger than feather atoms
A suitcase of lead has more mass in the same volume
The lead suitcase is physically larger

quizPool.prompt: If you have a balloon the size of a house and a small marble made of lead, which is denser?
quizPool.explanation: Density isn't about total size; it's about how tightly packed the matter is. The lead marble packs more mass into a tiny space.
quizPool.learnMoreText: 🎥 Watch: High Density vs Low Density

quizPool.prompt: Why did the heavy rock fall through the canvas bag in the pantry?
quizPool.explanation: Because of its high density, the rock exerted a huge amount of pressure on a very small area of the canvas, tearing it.

options.label: The bag was made of paper

quizPool.prompt: What happens to the atoms in a solid when it is heated past its melting point?
quizPool.explanation: The heat provides kinetic energy, breaking the atoms out of their rigid structure so they can slide past one another as a liquid.

options.label: They gain energy and start sliding around
They turn into a completely different element

quizPool.prompt: What analogy did Calculus use to describe atoms in a Solid state?
quizPool.explanation: He compared them to a 'Mosh Pit'—shoulders together, vibrating, but stationary and locked in a grid.

options.label: A Mosh Pit, vibrating but stationary

quizPool.prompt: When the Zlatanium rock melted in the water, was it a chemical change or a physical change?
quizPool.explanation: It was a physical change of state! The atoms are still Zlatanium, just moving differently.

quizPool.prompt: If you turn the heat off and let liquid silver cool down until it becomes a solid again, what is the process called?
quizPool.explanation: Turning a liquid into a solid by removing heat (energy) is called freezing or solidification.

quizPool.prompt: Why did the liquid Zlatanium turn into a gas when Captain Haddock left the stove on high?
quizPool.explanation: It reached its Boiling Point. The atoms gained so much kinetic energy they broke completely free from each other.

options.label: It reacted with the copper pot
It was destroyed by the heat
It turned into steam from the water

quizPool.prompt: What happens during Condensation?
quizPool.explanation: Condensation occurs when a gas hits a cooler surface, loses kinetic energy, and turns back into a liquid.

options.label: A liquid turns into a solid
A gas loses energy and becomes a liquid
A solid skips the liquid phase and becomes a gas

quizPool.prompt: Why did the silver cloche get hot when the Zlatanium gas condensed on it?
quizPool.explanation: As the gas turns back into a liquid, it must release the thermal energy it originally absorbed from the stove.

options.label: The gas releases energy as it becomes a liquid
The cloche was made of copper
Friction from the gas hitting the metal
The ice under it was actually dry ice

quizPool.prompt: When the Zlatanium became a 'silver fog', did it lose any of its actual mass?
quizPool.explanation: No! According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, the atoms are exactly the same, they are just spread much further apart.

options.label: No, the atoms are just further apart and moving faster
No, but the atoms shrank in size

quizPool.prompt: If you have ice, water, and steam, in which state are the atoms moving the FASTEST?
quizPool.explanation: In a gas (steam), atoms have the most kinetic energy, meaning they are zooming around and moving the fastest.
quizPool.learnMoreText: 🎥 Watch: Kinetic Energy in States of Matter

options.label: They move at the same speed

quizPool.prompt: According to Professor Calculus, what are atoms?
quizPool.explanation: Atoms are the indivisible building blocks of matter, like the pixels in a photograph or individual LEGO bricks.
quizPool.learnMoreText: 🔗 Explore: The Building Blocks of Matter

options.label: Tiny invisible solar systems that make up all matter
Drops of liquid frozen in time

quizPool.prompt: Why couldn't the Thomsons saw through the Zlatanium cube with a diamond saw?
quizPool.explanation: They were trying to saw through the atoms themselves. Atoms are the fundamental 'bricks' of the metal and cannot be simply sliced.
quizPool.learnMoreText: 🎥 Watch: Can You Cut an Atom?

options.label: The saw was out of gas
You cannot break the fundamental atomic 'bricks' with a physical saw
The cube was made of liquid

quizPool.prompt: What did John Dalton teach us about atoms of different elements?
quizPool.explanation: Dalton theorized that atoms of different elements have different weights, sizes, and chemical properties.

options.label: They are all exactly the same
They have different weights and properties
They frequently change into one another

quizPool.prompt: How did Tintin dislodge the 'misfit' Magnesium atom from the silver cube?
quizPool.explanation: Because it was a different weight, it had a different resonant frequency. Vibrating it at that exact rhythm shook it loose.

options.label: He melted it with a blowtorch
He matched its resonant frequency with vibrations

quizPool.prompt: When the Magnesium strip burned in the sun, turning into ash and smoke, did its overall mass disappear?
quizPool.explanation: No! The Law of Conservation of Mass states that in a chemical reaction, matter is neither created nor destroyed, only rearranged.

options.label: No, the atoms just moved into the ash and the air
No, but the atoms became lighter

quizPool.prompt: Why did the tray on the scale become lighter after the Magnesium flashed?
quizPool.explanation: Some of the atoms drifted away as smoke (a gas). If the smoke was captured in a vacuum jar, the weight would perfectly balance.

options.label: The atoms escaped as gas into the open air
The scale was broken by the light

quizPool.prompt: How did Professor Calculus explain the difference between a Mixture and a Compound?
quizPool.explanation: He compared a Mixture to a Salad (where ingredients just touch) and a Compound to a Soup (where ingredients are chemically bonded).

options.label: A Mixture is hot, a Compound is cold
A Mixture is like a Salad, a Compound is like a blended Soup
A Compound is always a liquid

quizPool.prompt: Why was Tintin able to pull the iron filings out of the sludge with a magnet?
quizPool.explanation: The sludge was a Mixture, meaning the iron atoms kept their original magnetic properties because they hadn't chemically bonded with the sand.

options.label: Iron atoms are stronger than sand
In a mixture, elements retain their physical properties

quizPool.prompt: How can you separate solid sand from blue crystals that have dissolved in water?
quizPool.explanation: You use Filtration. The water and dissolved crystals pass through the filter paper, but the larger solid sand particles are trapped.

options.label: By pouring it through filter paper

quizPool.prompt: After filtering out the sand, how do you get the blue crystals back out of the water?
quizPool.explanation: By applying heat, the water evaporates (turns to gas), leaving the solid blue crystals behind in the beaker.

options.label: Add more sand to soak it up

quizPool.prompt: What is an Element, like the gold plate found at the bottom of the mixture?
quizPool.explanation: An Element is a pure substance where every single atom is of the exact same type. It cannot be separated into anything simpler.

options.label: A substance made of many different mixed atoms
A substance where every single 'brick' (atom) is the exact same type
A liquid that has turned into a gas
